source_text: σουσι. Καὶ θῄσεις αὐτὰς ἐν τῇ σκηνῇ τοῦ μαρτυρίου, κατέναντι τοῦ μαρτυρίου, ἐν οἷς γνωσθήσομαί σοι ἐκεῖ. Καὶ ἔσται, ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὃν ἂν ἐκλέξωμαι αὐτὸν, ἡ ῥάβδος αὐτοῦ ἐκβλαστήσει. Καὶ περιελῶ ἀπ' ἐμοῦ τὸν γογγυσμὸν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ, ἃ αὐτοὶ γογγύζουσιν ἐφ' ὑμῖν. Καὶ ἐλάλησε Μωσῆς τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ ἔδωκαν αὐτῷ πάντες οἱ ἄρχοντες αὐτῶν ῥάβδον, τῷ ἄρχοντι τῷ ἑνὶ ῥάβδον κατ' ἄρχοντα, κατ' οἴκους πατριῶν αὐτῶν, δώδεκα ῥάβδους. Καὶ ἡ ῥάβδος Ἀαρὼν ἀναμέσον τῶν ῥάβδων αὐτῶν, καὶ ἀπέθηκε Μωσῆς τὰς ῥάβδους ἔναντι Κυρίου ἐν τῇ σκηνῇ τοῦ μαρτυρίου. Καὶ ἐγένετο τῇ ἐπαύριον, καὶ εἰσῆλθε Μωσῆς καὶ Ἀαρὼν ἐν τῇ σκηνῇ τοῦ μαρτυρίου. Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐβλάστησεν ἡ ῥάβδος Ἀαρὼν εἰς οἶκον Λευῒ, καὶ ἐξήνεγκε βλαστὸν, καὶ ἐξήνθησεν ἄνθη, καὶ ἐβλάστησε κάρυα. Καὶ ἐξήνεγκε Μωσῆς πάσας τὰς ῥάβδους ἀπὸ προσώπου Κυρίου πρὸς πάντας υἱοὺς Ἰσραήλ. Καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἔλαβον ἕκαστος τῆν ῥάβδον αὐτοῦ. Καὶ εἶπε Κύριος πρὸς Μωσῆν· Ἀπόθες τὴν ῥάβδον Ἀαρὼν ἐνώπιον τῶν μαρτυρίων εἰς διατήρησιν, σημεῖον τοῖς υἱοῖς τῶν ἀνηκόων. Καὶ παυσάσθω ὁ γογγυσμὸς αὐτῶν ἀπ' ἐμοῦ, καὶ οὐ μὴ ἀποθάνωσι.» Σημεῖον οὖν οὐκ ἀσυμφανὲς τοῦ ἐξῃρῆσθαι λαμπρῶς καὶ ἐκκεκριμένως εἰς ἱερουργίαν, ὡς ἐξ αἵματος Λευῒ, τὸν θεσπέσιον Ἀαρὼν, τὸ ἐξανθῆσαι τὴν ῥάβδον. Περιτρεπομένης δὲ αὖθις εἰς θεωρίαν πνευματικὴν, ὡς ἐν τύποις ἔτι παχυτάτοις, τὸ Χριστοῦ μυστήριον ἀναλάμψει πάλιν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Τίνα τρόπον; {ΚΥΡ.} Κεχειροτόνηται μὲν γὰρ νομοθέτης ἅμα καὶ ἀρχιερεὺς ἐφ' ἡμᾶς παρὰ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρὸς ὁ Ἐμμανουὴλ, ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν προσκομιῶν τὸ θῦμα. Ὡς γὰρ ὁ μακάριος ἔφη Παῦλος, «Ὁ μὲν νόμος διὰ Μωσέως, ἀνθρώπους καθίστησιν ἀρχιερεῖς ἔχοντας ἀσθένειαν· ὁ λόγος δὲ τῆς ὁρκωμοσίας τῆς μετὰ τὸν νόμον, Υἱὸν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τετελειωμένον.» Οὐκοῦν καθίκετο μὲν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ὁ Λόγος, καὶ γέγονε καθ' ἡμᾶς, τῶν ἁγίων λειτουργὸς καὶ τῆς σκηνῆς τῆς ἀληθινῆς ἣν ἔπηξεν ὁ Κύριος, καὶ οὐκ ἄνθρωπος. Ἀλλ' οὐκ ἐδόκει φρονεῖν ὀρθὰ τοῖς ἐξ αἵματος Ἰσραήλ· ἀντεξάγοντες δὲ ὥσπερ αὐτῷ τὸ ἴδιον θέλημα τοῖς ἐκ φθόνου βέλεσι πολυτρόπως ἔβαλλον, οὐ γλώττης, οὐ θράσους, οὐκ ἐκτόπων ἐπιχειρημάτων ἔτι φειδόμενοι, διολλύντες δὲ σφᾶς αὐτοὺς οἱ δείλαιοι, καὶ τελευταῖον ἐσταύρωσαν. Πλὴν ἀνέθαλλεν ἡ ῥάβδος ἡ ἐκ ῥίζης Ἰεσσαί· ἀνέφυ γὰρ δὴ καὶ ἀνεβίω Χριστὸς, λύσας τὰς ὀδύνας τοῦ θανάτου, καθὰ γέγραπται· ζωὴν γὰρ ὄντα κατὰ φύσιν, ὡς Θεὸν, πῶς ἦν εἰκὸς κρατεῖσθαι θανάτῳ, καὶ οὐχὶ δὴ μᾶλλον καταθλῆσαι φθορᾶς; Ὥσπερ δὲ τὸ ἀναφῦναι τὴν ῥάβδον, καὶ ἀναβλαστεῖν ἀδοκήτως τὸ ἀνανθὲς ἤδη ξύλον, διαρκὲς τοῖς ἀρχαιοτέροις σημεῖον ἦν τοῦ διὰ ψήφου τῆς ἄνωθεν εἰς ἀρχιερέα κεχειροτονῆσθαι τὸν Ἀαρών· οὕτω φαμὲν, ὅτι λαμπρά τε καὶ ἐναργὴς καὶ ἀποχρῶσα λίαν ἀπόδειξις τοῦ καὶ Θεὸν εἶναι κατὰ φύσιν τὸν Ἐμμανουὴλ, τὸ πατῆσαι θάνατον, καὶ ἀναβιῶναι θεοπρεπῶς. Καὶ γοῦν αὐτὸς ὁ Χριστὸς, καίτοι
pass_a_gloss: [Cont. quotation, Num 17:4–10 Eng. = LXX 17:19–25] …they will give. And you will set (τίθημι) them in the tent of the testimony (σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου), opposite the testimony, in which I will be made known (γνωσθήσομαι) to you there. And it will be: the man whom I choose (ἐκλέγομαι), his rod will sprout out (ἐκβλαστάνω). And I will take away (περιαιρέω) from me the murmuring (γογγυσμός) of the sons of Israel, which they murmur (γογγύζω) against you. Moses spoke to the sons of Israel and all their rulers gave him a rod, to each ruler a rod, by their fathers' houses, twelve rods; and Aaron's rod in the midst of their rods. Moses laid up (ἀποτίθημι) the rods before the Lord in the tent of testimony. And on the morrow (ἐπαύριον) Moses and Aaron went into the tent of the testimony; and behold Aaron's rod sprouted (βλαστάνω) for the house of Levi, brought out a shoot (βλαστός), flowered flowers (ἐξανθέω ἄνθη), and sprouted nuts (κάρυα). Moses brought out all the rods from the face of the Lord to all the sons of Israel; they saw and each took his rod. The Lord said to Moses: Lay up Aaron's rod before the testimonies for keeping, a sign (σημεῖον) for the sons of the disobedient (ἀνήκοοι); and let their murmuring cease from me, and they shall not die (οὐ μὴ ἀποθάνωσι). — A sign, then, not unclear (οὐκ ἀσυμφανές), of the divine (θεσπέσιος) Aaron's having been picked out (ἐξαιρέω, pf.) brilliantly and selectively (ἐκκεκριμένως) for sacred service (ἱερουργία), as of the blood of Levi, was the rod's blossoming out (ἐξανθῆσαι). But [the matter] being turned (περιτρέπω) again to spiritual contemplation (θεωρία πνευματική), as in still very thick (παχύτατος) types, the mystery (μυστήριον) of Christ will shine up (ἀναλάμπω) again. — PALL.: In what manner? — CYR.: For Emmanuel has been elected (χειροτονέω, pf. pass.) lawgiver (νομοθέτης) and at once high priest (ἀρχιερεύς) over/for us (ἐφ' ἡμᾶς) by God and Father, about to offer (προσκομίζω, fut. ptc.) himself as the victim (θῦμα) for us. As blessed Paul said: The law through Moses establishes (καθίστημι) men as high priests having weakness (ἀσθένεια); but the word of the oath-taking (ὁρκωμοσία) after the law, a Son perfected (τελειόω) for ever [Heb 7:28]. So the Word came down (καθικνέομαι) from heaven and came to be as we are, minister (λειτουργός) of the holy things and of the true tent which the Lord fixed (πήγνυμι), not man [Heb 8:2]. But it did not seem good (οὐκ ἐδόκει) to those of the blood of Israel to think rightly (φρονεῖν ὀρθά); bringing out against him (ἀντεξάγω) as it were their own will (θέλημα), they struck (βάλλω) him variously (πολυτρόπως) with the darts (βέλη) of envy (φθόνος), no longer sparing (φείδομαι) tongue, boldness, or outlandish (ἔκτοπος) attempts (ἐπιχειρήματα), destroying (διόλλυμι) themselves, the wretched (δείλαιοι), and at last crucified (σταυρόω) [him]. Yet the rod from the root of Jesse sprouted again (ἀναθάλλω) [Isa 11:1]; for Christ grew up again (ἀναφύω) and came to life again (ἀναβιόω), having loosed (λύω) the pangs (ὠδῖνες) of death, as written [Acts 2:24]; for being life (ζωή) by nature (κατὰ φύσιν), as God, how was it likely he be held (κρατέομαι) by death, and not rather overcome (καταθλέω) corruption (φθορά)? As the rod's growing up again and the already flowerless (ἀνανθής) wood (ξύλον) sprouting again unexpectedly (ἀδοκήτως) was a sufficient (διαρκής) sign to the more ancient ones of Aaron's having been elected high priest through the vote from above, so we say that a brilliant, evident (ἐναργής) and very sufficient (ἀποχρῶσα) proof (ἀπόδειξις) of Emmanuel's being also God by nature is his trampling (πατέω) death and living again in a God-befitting way (θεοπρεπῶς). And indeed Christ himself, although [continues §14].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …give them. And you shall set them in the tent of witness, before the testimony, where I will make myself known to you. And the rod of the man whom I choose shall sprout; and I will take away from me the grumbling of the sons of Israel, which they grumble against you. And Moses spoke to the sons of Israel, and all their leaders gave him a rod, one rod for each leader, according to their fathers’ houses, twelve rods; and Aaron’s rod was among their rods. And Moses laid up the rods before the Lord in the tent of witness. And on the next day Moses and Aaron went into the tent of witness; and behold, Aaron’s rod for the house of Levi had sprouted, and put forth a shoot, and burst into flower, and borne almonds. And Moses brought out all the rods from the presence of the Lord to all the sons of Israel; and they looked, and each man took his own rod. And the Lord said to Moses: Lay up Aaron’s rod before the testimonies, to be kept as a sign for the sons of the disobedient; and let their grumbling against me cease, so that they do not die’ (Numbers 17:3–10). So the blossoming of the rod was no obscure sign that the inspired Aaron, as one of the blood of Levi, had been chosen with distinction and set apart for the priestly service. But when the account is turned once more to spiritual contemplation, the mystery of Christ will shine out again, though still, as it were, in very coarse types.

Cyril: Emmanuel has been appointed for us by God the Father as Lawgiver and High Priest at once, to offer himself for us as the sacrifice. For as blessed Paul said: ‘The law through Moses appoints as high priests men who have weakness; but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son made perfect for ever’ (Hebrews 7:28). So the Word came down from heaven and became one of us, ‘a minister of the sanctuary and of the true tent, which the Lord pitched, and not man’ (Hebrews 8:2). But those of the blood of Israel did not see fit to think rightly. Setting their own will against him, as it were, they shot at him in many ways with the arrows of envy, no longer holding back their tongues, their insolence or their outrageous schemes; and the wretches, destroying themselves, at last crucified him. Yet the rod from the root of Jesse (Isaiah 11:1) blossomed again. For Christ sprang up again and came back to life, ‘having loosed the pangs of death’ (Acts 2:24), as it is written. Since he is Life by nature, as God, how could he be held by death (Acts 2:24), and not rather triumph over corruption? Just as the springing up of the rod, when wood already past flowering unexpectedly sprouted again, was a sufficient sign to the people of old that Aaron had been appointed high priest by decree from above, so we say that his trampling on death and coming back to life as befits God is a clear, plain and fully sufficient proof that Emmanuel is also God by nature. Indeed Christ himself, although…

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-word (δώ|σουσι), finishing the quotation begun in §12. Numbers 17:3–10 in English numbering = LXX Numbers 17:18–25 (‘…give them’ ends 17:3 = LXX 17:18) (the LXX counts English 16:36–50 as 17:1–15). κάρυα means ‘nuts’ in Greek; rendered ‘almonds’ with the Hebrew and the English Bibles, which also prepares for the almond rod of Jeremiah 1:11 in §14. σημεῖον τοῖς υἱοῖς τῶν ἀνηκόων rendered ‘a sign for the sons of the disobedient’ (Hebrew: ‘rebels’). καὶ οὐ μὴ ἀποθάνωσι rendered ‘so that they do not die’; the strong negation is kept. ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς with κεχειροτόνηται rendered ‘for us’ (it could also be ‘over us’). ‘Lawgiver’ is capitalised as a title of Christ next to ‘High Priest’. Hebrews 7:28: Cyril adds ‘through Moses’ (διὰ Μωσέως) and attributes Hebrews to Paul; both kept. Hebrews 8:2: τῶν ἁγίων rendered ‘the sanctuary’. Isaiah 11:1 LXX has ῥάβδος (‘rod’) from the root of Jesse, which is why Cyril links it to Aaron’s rod; ‘rod’ kept to keep the link. Acts 2:24 is quoted (‘having loosed the pangs of death’) and then alluded to (‘how could he be held by death’), so it is cited at both places. ἐν τύποις ἔτι παχυτάτοις: ‘very coarse types’ (παχύς, thick, gross) means figures still thick and material, not yet transparent. ‘Did not see fit to think rightly’ renders οὐκ ἐδόκει φρονεῖν ὀρθά. No citation is given for the crucifixion summary, which is narrative and not a quotation. Reviewer: προσκομιῶν is a future participle of purpose, so ‘to offer himself’ replaces ‘offering himself’.
